reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is presented as an instructional walkthrough for checking eligibility and claiming a described SOL airdrop through a wallet. It includes safety guidance not to share a seed phrase and identifies wallet connection as the stated requirement. Although it shows a reward, wallet-address form, and adjacent password prompt, those cues alone are insufficient to establish deceptive conduct.

opening.argument: The central promise is a free 10 SOL reward, and it is directly tied to a sequence of actions on an external site. The video tells viewers to visit the linked destination, submit a Solana wallet address, verify it, and then confirm a claim transaction. The claimed benefit is not merely discussed: the presenter says the address is eligible for 10 SOL and instructs viewers to click the claim button. That is a low-barrier asset-acquisition solicitation in which wallet interaction is the condition for pursuing the promised reward.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this an instructional walkthrough does not answer what viewers are being instructed to do. The cited safety language concerns seed phrases, but the actual flow still directs viewers to an external claim site, enter a wallet address, verify it, and confirm a transaction. “No staking or deposits” narrows the claimed requirement; it does not remove the solicitation or establish that the promised reward is genuine.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The action sequence is presented as a standard eligibility check and wallet claim, not proof of deception. The description expressly says no staking or deposits are required and warns viewers never to share a seed phrase. The quoted material shows a wallet address and transaction confirmation, but it does not show that funds were taken, that credentials were requested, or that the reward was fabricated.

opening.argument: Several concrete risk signals reinforce one another: the offer is an unusually easy 10 SOL reward, the claim is routed through an external URL, and participation involves a wallet address and transaction confirmation. The page also presents institutional-sounding assurances alongside the claim flow, including “Official Solana Partner” and “Audit by CertiK,” while a wallet-unlock panel is visible during the eligibility sequence. These cues make the offer appear validated and low-risk while steering viewers toward wallet-related actions. The combination is materially more concerning than an ordinary reward announcement.

citations.quote: my address is eligible for 10 sol

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference treats the wallet and reward cues as isolated, but the relevant issue is their combination. A safety warning does not explain why a large free-token claim is paired with an external destination, verification, transaction confirmation, and visible wallet-unlock context. Nor does labeling the page instructional establish that its institutional-looking assurances are authentic or that the displayed reward is actually available.

citations.quote: Never share your seed phrase.
the 10 SOL has already arrived in my wallet

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These signals remain suggestive rather than conclusive. The supplied material does not show a seed phrase being requested, a deposit being demanded, or a loss occurring. The visible wallet panel and branded page establish only what was displayed, while the description states that no staking or deposits are required and identifies wallet connection as the requirement. Apparent authority cues alone do not prove a scam.

opening.argument: Although presented as education, the video functions as a direct promotional funnel. Its title promises a step-by-step method to claim free SOL, the description supplies a “Claim here” URL, and the narration tells viewers to check whether the airdrop is available for them. The presenter then asks viewers to comment how much SOL they claim and subscribe for more crypto opportunities. This is not detached reporting about an airdrop; it actively directs participation in a specific claim flow and encourages further audience acquisition around similar offers.

citations.quote: Step-by-Step Guide to Claim Free $SOL
Claim here: https://msolcore.xyz/
Now you can also check if this airdrop is available for you
Write in the comments how much SOL you claim.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The presence of instructional content does not make the content neutral. The title promises free SOL, the description puts the destination immediately beside the claim, and the narration explicitly invites viewers to perform the same check and report their claimed amount. “Subscribe” and “like” are ordinary engagement requests, but here they accompany a specific crypto participation pathway rather than merely explaining a general concept.

citations.quote: Claim Free $SOL (Phantom Wallet)
Claim here: https://msolcore.xyz/
Now you can also check if this airdrop is available for you

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Instructional promotion is compatible with an ordinary rewards campaign and does not itself establish fraud. The material identifies the subject as a free-token airdrop and explains an eligibility process; it does not claim that viewers must pay or invest. The call to comment and subscribe is audience engagement, while the stated offer says no staking or deposits are required.
